In [[descriptive set theory]], a set <math>S</math> is said to be '''homogeneously Suslin''' if it is the projection of a [[homogeneous tree|homogeneous]] [[tree (descriptive set theory)|tree]]. <math>S</math> is said to be '''<math>\kappa</math>-homogeneously Suslin''' if it is the projection of a <math>\kappa</math>-homogeneous tree.

If <math>A\subseteq{}^\omega\omega</math> is a <math>\mathbf{\Pi}_1^1</math> set and <math>\kappa</math> is a measurable cardinal, then <math>A</math> is <math>\kappa</math>-homogeneously Suslin. This result is important in the proof that the existence of a [[measurable cardinal]] implies that <math>\mathbf{\Pi}_1^1</math> sets are [[determinacy|determined]].
